pr.title: fix(comm): compute the Lamport clear sub-buffer offset in 64 bits
pr.body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The Lamport all-reduce kernels return wrong sums on a workspace whose sub-buffer (`comm_size`) is larger than 1 GiB. No error is raised.

**Why**

- The Lamport workspace holds three sub-buffers of `comm_size` bytes. Each call writes one and clears the one from two calls back, at `clear_offset * comm_size`.
- That product was computed in `int`. With `clear_offset == 2` it passes 2^31 once `comm_size` exceeds 1 GiB, so the kernel cleared a wrong address and left the intended sub-buffer with stale data. A later one-shot call reading that sub-buffer takes the stale values as arrived.
- The data offset on the line above was already widened to `int64_t`; the clear offset was not.
- `comm_size = world_size * max_token_num * hidden_dim * 2` bytes (4 for fp32), capped just under 2 GiB by `MAX_COMM_SIZE`, so 1 to 2 GiB is an accepted configuration. Example: 8 ranks, hidden 8192, `max_token_num` 8192.

**What**

- `trtllm_allreduce_fusion.cuh`, `trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion.cuh`: the clear offset is computed in `int64_t`.
- New `tests/comm/test_trtllm_allreduce_fusion_large_workspace.py`: 2 ranks, `comm_size` 1.04 GiB, nine one-shot calls on one workspace with new inputs on every call, each compared with a PyTorch reference. Two cases, one per kernel: the plain all-reduce and the MoE finalize all-reduce. Needs 4.2 GiB per rank and skips without it. Enrolled in the multi-GPU job.

**Origin**

Found while reading TensorRT-LLM [#10499](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/10499) ([7d16f3a28](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/commit/7d16f3a28bd61e0d4bce28e789265083266ac025)), which makes `comm_size` 64-bit upstream. This PR takes only the part that is wrong in FlashInfer today. It does not lift the 2 GiB cap: the generated cake all-reduce kernels on the same workspace read `comm_size` as `int`. Their clear offset is already 64-bit.

GB200, 4-GPU node, CI container (CUDA 13.0), the new test file:

| Kernel | Without the fix | With the fix |
|---|---|---|
| All-reduce | fails at call 5: 126,669 of 131,072 elements wrong, largest difference 6.57 | passes |
| MoE finalize all-reduce | fails: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access` | passes |

Measured at `410bf315c`; the two later commits change only how the test starts and stops its rank processes. "Without the fix" is the same tree with the fix commit reverted. A separate run on main with four workspace sizes (nine all-reduce calls each, 2 ranks): 64 MiB and 0.92 GiB all correct; 1.04 GiB and 1.83 GiB each have one wrong call per rank, about 112,700 of 131,072 elements.

**Performance: no measurable change.** The fix widens one multiply that each thread runs once at kernel entry, outside any loop; below 1 GiB the address it computes is the same as before.

One-shot all-reduce, bf16, hidden 7168, 16 tokens, GB200. Old and new expression built side by side from one tree and alternated (old, new, new, old; three rounds), 600 timed calls per run, per-call GPU time on rank 0:

| Ranks | Old, median per run (us) | New, median per run (us) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 47, 46, 46, 57, 61, 46 | 47, 54, 47, 58, 47, 48 |
| 4 | 48, 44, 44, 59, 47, 57 | 58, 58, 43, 64, 62, 44 |

A run of either build settles near 45 us or near 58 us, so the spread between runs of one build (about 15 us) is far larger than any difference between the builds. The fastest runs agree to within 1 us (2 ranks: 46 vs 47; 4 ranks: 44 vs 43). 1 and 128 tokens look the same.

The existing MoE finalize test would not show this even on a large workspace: it passes the same inputs on every call, so stale Lamport data equals the right answer.

+"""One-shot Lamport kernels on a workspace whose sub-buffer exceeds 1 GiB.
+
+The Lamport workspace holds three sub-buffers of ``comm_size`` bytes; each call
+writes one and clears the one two calls back. Above 1 GiB the byte offset of the
+third sub-buffer (``2 * comm_size``) no longer fits in a 32-bit int. Every call
+gets new inputs, so a sub-buffer left with the data of an earlier call shows.
+"""
+
+import multiprocessing as mp
+import socket
+import sys
+import time
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+
+import flashinfer.comm as comm
+from flashinfer.comm.mnnvl import TorchDistBackend
+
+WORLD_SIZE = 2
+HIDDEN = 8192
+# comm_size = world_size * max_token_num * hidden * 2 bytes = 1.04 GiB.
+MAX_TOKEN_NUM = 34000
+TOKENS = 16
+# Enough calls for every sub-buffer to be reused after a clear at offset 2.
+NUM_CALLS = 9
+# Lamport sub-buffers (3 * comm_size) plus the two-shot buffer (comm_size).
+REQUIRED_BYTES_PER_RANK = 4 * WORLD_SIZE * MAX_TOKEN_NUM * HIDDEN * 2
+# Exit code of a rank whose TCPStore port was taken between _get_open_port and its own bind.
+PORT_IN_USE_EXIT_CODE = 98
+MAX_PORT_ATTEMPTS = 3
+
+
+def _get_open_port() -> int:
+    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as sock:
+        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+        return sock.getsockname()[1]
+
+
+def _init_process_group(rank: int, port: int, backend: str = "nccl") -> None:
+    try:
+        dist.init_process_group(
+            backend=backend,
+            init_method=f"tcp://localhost:{port}",
+            rank=rank,
+            world_size=WORLD_SIZE,
+        )
+    except RuntimeError as error:
+        if "EADDRINUSE" in str(error) or "address already in use" in str(error):
+            sys.exit(PORT_IN_USE_EXIT_CODE)
+        raise
+
+
+def _run_ranks(worker) -> None:
+    """Run one process per rank; on a taken port, start over on a new one."""
+    ctx = mp.get_context("spawn")
+    for _ in range(MAX_PORT_ATTEMPTS):
+        port = _get_open_port()
+        procs = [
+            ctx.Process(target=worker, args=(rank, port)) for rank in range(WORLD_SIZE)
+        ]
+        for proc in procs:
+            proc.start()
+        # A rank that exits early leaves its peers in the unbounded Lamport
+        # wait (or waiting on the store), so stop them instead of joining.
+        while any(p.is_alive() for p in procs) and all(
+            p.exitcode in (None, 0) for p in procs
+        ):
+            time.sleep(0.2)
+        failed = any(p.exitcode not in (None, 0) for p in procs)
+        port_in_use = any(p.exitcode == PORT_IN_USE_EXIT_CODE for p in procs)
+        for proc in procs:
+            if failed and proc.is_alive():
+                proc.kill()
+            proc.join()
+        if not port_in_use:
+            break
+    exit_codes = [proc.exitcode for proc in procs]
+    assert all(code == 0 for code in exit_codes), f"rank exit codes: {exit_codes}"
+
+
+def _worker(rank: int, port: int) -> None:
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+    torch.cuda.set_device(device)
+    _init_process_group(rank, port)
+    group = dist.group.WORLD
+    workspace = None
+    try:
+        workspace = comm.create_allreduce_fusion_workspace(
+            backend="trtllm",
+            world_size=WORLD_SIZE,
+            rank=rank,
+            max_token_num=MAX_TOKEN_NUM,
+            hidden_dim=HIDDEN,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            comm_backend=TorchDistBackend(group=group),
+        )
+        for call in range(NUM_CALLS):
+            torch.manual_seed(100 * call + rank)
+            x = torch.randn(TOKENS, HIDDEN, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            ref = x.float().clone()
+            dist.all_reduce(ref, group=group)
+            out = torch.empty_like(x)
+            comm.allreduce_fusion(
+                input=x,
+                workspace=workspace,
+                pattern=comm.AllReduceFusionPattern.kAllReduce,
+                output=out,
+                use_oneshot=True,
+            )
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                out.float(),
+                ref,
+                atol=5e-2,
+                rtol=1e-2,
+                msg=lambda m: f"call {call}: {m}",
+            )
+    finally:
+        if workspace is not None:
+            workspace.destroy()
+        if dist.is_initialized():
+            dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+def _moe_finalize_worker(rank: int, port: int) -> None:
+    """The MoE finalize all-reduce, which has its own copy of the Lamport helper."""
+    device = torch.device(f"cuda:{rank}")
+    torch.cuda.set_device(device)
+    _init_process_group(rank, port)
+    group = dist.group.WORLD
+    ipc_handles = None
+    try:
+        ipc_handles, workspace_tensor = (
+            comm.trtllm_create_ipc_workspace_for_all_reduce_fusion(
+                rank, WORLD_SIZE, MAX_TOKEN_NUM, HIDDEN, group=group
+            )
+        )
+        dtype, top_k = torch.bfloat16, 8
+        for call in range(NUM_CALLS):
+            # The same inputs on every rank, new ones on every call.
+            gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(call)
+            shared = torch.randn(TOKENS, HIDDEN, generator=gen).to(device, dtype)
+            fc2 = torch.randn(TOKENS * top_k, HIDDEN, generator=gen).to(device, dtype)
+            scale = torch.randn(TOKENS, top_k, generator=gen).to(device, dtype)
+            idx = torch.randint(
+                0, TOKENS * top_k, (TOKENS, top_k), generator=gen, dtype=torch.int32
+            ).to(device)
+            residual = torch.randn(TOKENS, HIDDEN, generator=gen).to(device, dtype)
+            norm_weight = torch.randn(HIDDEN, generator=gen).to(device, dtype)
+            norm_out = torch.empty_like(residual)
+            residual_out = torch.empty_like(residual)
+            quant_out = torch.empty(TOKENS * HIDDEN // 4, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+            scale_out = torch.empty(
+                comm.compute_fp4_swizzled_layout_sf_size(TOKENS, HIDDEN // 16),
+                dtype=torch.uint8,
+                device=device,
+            )
+            comm.trtllm_moe_finalize_allreduce_fusion(
+                allreduce_in=fc2,
+                residual_in=residual,
+                norm_weight=norm_weight,
+                expanded_idx_to_permuted_idx=idx,
+                workspace_ptrs=workspace_tensor,
+                launch_with_pdl=False,
+                world_rank=rank,
+                world_size=WORLD_SIZE,
+                eps=1e-5,
+                shared_expert_output=shared,
+                expert_scale_factor=scale,
+                norm_out=norm_out,
+                residual_out=residual_out,
+                quant_out=quant_out,
+                scale_out=scale_out,
+                routed_scaling_factor=1.0,
+            )
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            per_rank = (
+                torch.sum(fc2[idx].float() * scale.unsqueeze(-1).float(), dim=1)
+                + shared.float()
+            ).to(dtype)
+            ref = (per_rank * WORLD_SIZE + residual).float()
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                residual_out.float(),
+                ref,
+                atol=0.2,
+                rtol=0.2,
+                msg=lambda m: f"call {call}: {m}",
+            )
+    finally:
+        dist.barrier(group=group)
+        if ipc_handles is not None:
+            comm.trtllm_destroy_ipc_workspace_for_all_reduce_fusion(
+                ipc_handles, group=group
+            )
+        dist.destroy_process_group(group=group)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "worker",
+    [
+        pytest.param(_worker, id="allreduce"),
+        pytest.param(_moe_finalize_worker, id="moe_finalize"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_oneshot_comm_size_above_1gib(worker) -> None:
+    if torch.cuda.device_count() < WORLD_SIZE:
+        pytest.skip(f"requires at least {WORLD_SIZE} GPUs")
+    for rank in range(WORLD_SIZE):
+        free, _ = torch.cuda.mem_get_info(rank)
+        if free < REQUIRED_BYTES_PER_RANK + (2 << 30):
+            pytest.skip(
+                f"requires {REQUIRED_BYTES_PER_RANK / 2**30:.1f} GiB free on cuda:{rank}"
+            )
+    _run_ranks(worker)

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
